title: Bounded-above flat scalar-extension coordinates for canonical single base change at a stalk
statement: Let Y, B, A be schemes [def-pc-scheme], p:Y -> B quasi-compact and quasi-separated, M a quasi-coherent module [pqf-def-coherent] flat over p [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], g:A -> B, and a a point of A. Set R=O_B,g(a), T=O_A,a, and f=g_a:R -> T. Use the standard derived categories [def-pc-derived-category] and canonical single-module comparison beta [def-pc-standard-single-base-change-map]. There exist a cochain complex P of R-modules, an integer b with P^i=0 for i>b, and flatness of every P^i, a universal total left-derived scalar-extension functor LF and its counit epsilon, such that for every integer n there are T-linear isomorphisms eL from the stalk of H^n(source(beta)) to H^n(LF(Qh(P))) and eR from H^n(Qh(f_*(P))) to the stalk of H^n(target(beta)), where f_* here means ordinary extension of scalars. The stalk map [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] of H^n(beta) equals eL.hom followed by H^n(epsilon_P) followed by eR.hom. The statement gives coordinates and a commuting square; it assumes no invertibility or cancellation property of epsilon_P or beta.

proof.text: Work on affine neighbourhoods of g(a) and a. For an affine source chart, the degree-zero complex of sections of M is flat over the old base sections by relative flatness. The affine section tensor formula computes the pullback complex. The adjunction unit and counit equations identify the canonical base-change map with the scalar-extension counit; no invertibility of that counit is used.

For a quasi-compact separated source open, choose a finite affine cover. Finite intersections are affine. The finite alternating Cech complex computes its direct image and has flat terms. The elementary-tensor identifications on each intersection commute with restrictions and hence alternating differentials; they give the ordinary base-change cohomology identification and the counit square.

For a qcqs source use induction on a finite affine cover. At a union U with one affine V, U intersect V is a quasi-compact separated open of V, so the preceding Cech calculation applies. The relative Mayer--Vietoris triangle represents the union by the shifted cone of the two-open-to-overlap restriction map. Lift that map to bounded-above flat resolutions, replacing its terms by such resolutions when needed; finite sums and shifted cones remain flat and bounded above. Naturality of the unit/counit description gives the scalar-extension counit square on this cone. This constructs the model and its comparison identifications without assuming the comparison is invertible.

Localize the constructed complex at g(a). Flatness and the upper support bound survive. Extend to the local ring of A at a. Exactness of stalks identifies its cohomology with the two sheaf cohomology stalks and transports the counit square. Uniqueness of the universal left-derived scalar-extension pair permits any universal pair LF,epsilon in the coordinates. All witnesses are destructured only in proofs, never selected to define data.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_standardSingle_stalk_flat_counit_model
    {Y B A : Scheme.{u}} (p : Y ⟶ B) [QuasiCompact p] [QuasiSeparated p]
    (M : Y.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] (hM : M.IsFlatOver p) (g : A ⟶ B) (a : A) :
    letI := fun X : Scheme.{u} ↦ HasDerivedCategory.standard
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))
    let R := B.presheaf.stalk (g a)
    let T := A.presheaf.stalk a
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} R)
    letI := HasDerivedCategory.standard (ModuleCat.{u} T)
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ),
      (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (P.X i)) ∧
      (∀ i : ℤ, Module.Flat R (P.X i)) ∧
      ∃ (LF : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} T))
        (ε : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ LF ⟶
          (ModuleCat.extendScalars (g.stalkMap a).hom).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙
            DerivedCategory.Qh),
        LF.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)) ∧
        ∀ n : ℤ,
          ∃ (eL : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).obj
              ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
                ((derivedPullback g).obj ((schemeDerivedDirectImage p).obj
                  ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M)))) ≅
              (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
                (LF.obj (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
                  ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj P))))
            (eR : (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
                (DerivedCategory.Qh.obj
                  (((ModuleCat.extendScalars (g.stalkMap a).hom).mapHomotopyCategory
                    (.up ℤ)).obj ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj P))) ≅
              (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).obj
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).obj
                  ((schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd p g)).obj
                    ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj
                      (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullbackObj (pullback.fst p g) M))))),
            (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor A.toRingedSpace a).map
                ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).map (standardSingleBaseChangeMap p M g)) =
              eL.hom ≫ (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ n).map
                (ε.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ (.up ℤ)).obj P)) ≫ eR.hom
